newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan king departs for medical, talks in US.
newsitem.headline: Jordan king departs for medical, talks in US.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein left for the United States on Friday for a medical checkup and talks with U.S. President Clinton on the Middle East peace process, officials said.

They said the king, accompanied by his U.S. born wife Queen Noor, will go first for routine tests at the Mayo Clinic in Minnesota before talks in Washington with Clinton and senior adminstration officials.
King Hussein has returned annually to the clinic since surgery for cancer in 1992 with no apparent recurrence of the disease.

Officials said the talks in Washington later in the month would address tension in the Middle East after new Jewish settlement building on occupied Arab land by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government.

The monarch has helped defuse earlier Israeli-Palestinian tension. But Jordan, with a large Palestinian community, fears a new outbreak of violence that could threaten its own stability, officials say.
King Hussein's talks are also expected to cover Iraq, with many Jordanian officials privately complaining Washington does not have a clear policy.

Jordan, once a close ally of Iraqi President Saddam Hussein, has aligned itself with a U.S. policy against the Baghdad ruler. But Jordan now wishes to improve ties with Iraq to win sales under the U.N. "oil-for food" deal.

The Jordanian-U.S. talks follow an abrupt change of prime minister. The king last Wednesday brought back Abdul Salam al-Majali, who signed the peace treaty with Israel when he was prime minister in 1994.
The king, shocked by a Jordanian soldier's killing of seven Israeli schoolgirls on March 13, made a high-profile visit to Jerusalem to visit relatives of the dead.

Three days later he sacked Prime Minister Abdul Karim al-Kabariti, a move political observers linked to differences over Israel. They said the new cabinet, which includes many members of Jordan's peace negotiating team with Israel, showed the king's concern to deepen ties with Israel.
The king will assure U.S. leaders that Jordan's ties with Israel have not been jeopardised by the shooting by a member of the normally loyal armed forces, officials said.
